notebooks.title: Rational Responses to Epistemic Peer Disagreement
notebooks.summary: Epistemic disagreement occurs when agents with identical evidence reach different conclusions. These stances interact with Uniqueness and Permissivism; Uniqueness asserts that evidence dictates one correct rational attitude, whereas Permissivism allows for multiple. Current evidence suggests that unconditional deference (Conciliatory view) may be less tenable than a nuanced approach that accounts for case-specific conditions.
